subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should later operator `tools.exec` config changes take precedence over previously persisted `/exec` session defaults, and if so should existing persisted `exec*` session fields be migrated, reset, or made explicitly opt-in?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally support persistent authorized `/exec` session defaults, but the issue shows those defaults can shadow stricter later security policy; choosing precedence and migration semantics is a security/product contract decision.

options.title: Operator config wins with migration
options.body: Make stricter current config override or clear stale persisted `exec*` session defaults through a documented doctor/reset path, preserving explicit fresh `/exec` overrides only under the new policy.

options.title: Keep session defaults durable
options.body: Document that `/exec` session defaults intentionally outlive global config edits and provide an operator reset command or warning instead of changing precedence.

options.title: Remove durable exec session defaults
options.body: Stop persisting `/exec` fields and migrate existing entries away, accepting that prior per-session workflows no longer survive restarts.

recommendation.title: Operator config wins with migration
recommendation.body: Make stricter current config override or clear stale persisted `exec*` session defaults through a documented doctor/reset path, preserving explicit fresh `/exec` overrides only under the new policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The current behavior traces to the original `/exec` session override feature and later resolver coverage authored under this history.
